extracted.intended_audience: college faculty, department chairs, and administrators designing or assessing undergraduate quantitative reasoning/general-education programs
extracted.subtask_description: Program-level guidelines and course-level criteria for designing, selecting, and assessing undergraduate Quantitative Reasoning (QR) courses across the curriculum, with recommended learning outcomes, course descriptors, assessment tools, and curricular practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize Ideas Effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize Ideas Effectively. This includes using quantitative language and mathematical symbols to clarify ideas and using sketches, diagrams, graphs, tables, and other mathematical models to analyze situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the required first three areas students must develop in a course that will satisfy the Quantitative Reasoning requirement; emphasizes clarity of structure and use of quantitative representations to make ideas comprehensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate Ideas and Information Clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate Ideas and Information Clearly. This includes writing and speaking about quantitative ideas clearly in words, using mathematical notation correctly, presenting relevant data effectively, and using graphs and tables when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly foregrounded as a core skill (one of the first three). Courses should require students to express quantitative reasoning in multiple modalities (written, oral, symbolic, graphical).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct and Defend an Argument Using Evidence Persuasively
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct and Defend an Argument Using Evidence Persuasively. This includes reasoning deductively, using statistics appropriately, and using estimates and error analysis correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core outcome: students must be able to build a quantitative argument supported by evidence; includes use of statistical reasoning and attention to uncertainty and estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret and Create Graphs and Tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret and Create Graphs and Tables. This includes understanding Cartesian coordinates, converting information given by a formula, graph, or table to another format, understanding the significance of the slope and concavity of a graph, and understanding histograms and other ways to present data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes using software packages (Excel, Cricket Graph, Derive, Maple, Mathematica, MATLAB) to work with data presentation; listed as one of the competencies courses may require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Various Measurement Scales to Interpret Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Various Measurement Scales to Interpret Data. This includes converting between scales, converting units, and using appropriate scaling in graphs and tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical competency for interpreting numerical information presented in different scales or units; useful in cross-disciplinary contexts and modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply Simple Mathematical Models
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Simple Mathematical Models. This includes using various functions as mathematical models, and using algebra to make predictions from mathematical models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes modeling as a means to connect mathematics to real-world problems; courses should give practice in selecting and using simple functional models to make predictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret Statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret Statistics. This includes the understanding of mean, standard deviation, correlation coefficient, and regression lines, and using software packages such as Fastat, Minitab, and SPSS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical literacy is an explicit component; students should be able to compute and interpret common summary statistics and simple inferential tools, often via software.

rubrics_metrics.name: QR Course Satisfaction Rule (first-three + three-of-last-four)
rubrics_metrics.description: A course will satisfy the Quantitative Reasoning requirement if students in the course develop their ability in all of the first three areas, and three of the last four following areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program-level rule for certifying QR courses: all courses must cover the three communication/organization/argument outcomes and additionally achieve a threshold number of technical/data competencies (interpret/create graphs, measurement scales, modeling, statistics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize Conceptual Understanding and Modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses should stress conceptual understanding and apply mathematics in realistic contexts via modeling, using real-world data both as problem sources and motivation for mathematical developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as an overriding emphasis for curricular reform (developmental math through upper division); implies assignments that go beyond symbol manipulation to modeling and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of Technology and Software
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology has been integrated into all math offerings: graphing calculators are required in developmental through calculus courses; multivariable and advanced courses utilize Multigraph, Derive, Mathematica, MPP, Matlab; statistics use Minitab; other specialized packages used where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation that courses incorporate appropriate technology for computation, visualization, and data analysis; use of technology seen as essential to modern QR pedagogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Real-World Data and Project-Based Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Include student projects and assignments that go beyond template problems, using real-world data as sources of problems and motivation; students expected to conduct and write up individual/small group projects and make presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project-oriented assignments foster application, communication, and teamwork; cited across levels from precalculus to advanced courses and in interdisciplinary collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment Tool: Pre-Post Testing (strengths/weaknesses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-post testing: two equivalent multiple-choice exams were developed to test performance against the general QR skills list; administered on the first and last days of term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths: can measure skill gains objectively and easy to administer/track. Weaknesses: difficult to develop valid and reliable instruments in multiple versions; skills gained may be content-specific and not suited to a single exam across the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment Tool: Self-Reported Competencies, Attitudes, and Beliefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-Reported Assessment consisted of a forced-choice QR skill rating and open-end responses on attitudes toward the course and QR activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths: produces quantifiable perceived gains and sensible results, useful for instructor feedback. Weaknesses: perceived competencies may differ greatly from actual competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment Recommendation: Emphasize Learning Outcomes and Course-Specific Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assessment Committee recommends that ongoing assessment of QR should emphasize learning outcomes and is considering developing pre-post tests for specific courses or course clusters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggests shifting from a single program-wide multiple-choice test to outcome-aligned or course-cluster assessments to capture content-specific gains and better validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster Cross-disciplinary Connections and Transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: QR topics developed in one discipline should have relevance emphasized to other disciplines at the same time to improve transfer of skills between domains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies transfer as a known problem and recommends explicit cross-disciplinary linkage (e.g., when a topic is developed in Chemistry, emphasize relevance to Economics/Biology) to aid students in applying concepts in new contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutionalize Oversight and Faculty Awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional structures (e.g., a standing subcommittee of the Educational Policies Committee) are recommended to heighten faculty awareness of QR goals and provide oversight of the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without a body charged with oversight, program goals may be misunderstood or forgotten; institutionalization supports consistency, monitoring, and countering prejudices about program aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course Categorization and Accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: QR courses were initially categorized as 'q' (skill development) and 'Q' (application-oriented), with the goal that all students take a QR course appropriate to their preparation; distinctions later dropped but the intent remains to allow different entry points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program design should accommodate students with varying backgrounds (e.g., remedial skill-focused offerings and more advanced application courses) and provide advising/placement to guide choices.
